title: One change, two habitats
hook: The same habitat change can affect species differently.

knows: Animals depend on features of their surroundings.
doesNotKnow: A beaver dam turns part of a flowing channel into pond habitat. Which conclusion is best supported?

misconception: A single observation or change determines the same outcome everywhere.
objective: A beaver dam turns part of a flowing channel into pond habitat. Which conclusion is best supported?

claims.text: A beaver dam turns part of a flowing channel into pond habitat. Which conclusion is best supported? The panels distinguish a flowing-channel habitat from a pond habitat that can form upstream of a dam. Species differ in the conditions they use, so habitat change can create different benefits and costs. The drawing does not predict the abundance of a particular species.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: US Geological Survey, beavers and wetlands, https://www.usgs.gov/

claims.text: The panels show a simplified illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
A habitat gains standing water and loses some fast flow. What additional information is needed to assess an animal species? Species may depend on different features of the habitat.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: US Geological Survey, beavers and wetlands, https://www.usgs.gov/

recall.question: A habitat gains standing water and loses some fast flow. What additional information is needed to assess an animal species?
options: A guarantee that every species responds alike
recall.why: Species may depend on different features of the habitat.
